title: Salvation and Grace - Episode 4: Jesus Tasting Death's Bitter Cup for All

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Salvation and Grace. <chuckle> I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight we're thinking about a cup.
Not a cup of tea or wine at supper, but the cup Jesus spoke of in the garden, the one he asked the Father to take away if it were possible.
What was in that cup? <short pause> And why did he drink it?
The writer of Hebrews tells us something extraordinary.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Jesus tasted death for every person.
Not just observed it from a distance, not just made a gesture toward it, but tasted it.
The word carries the full experience, the bitterness, the weight of it. <short pause> He drank deeply from a cup that was meant for us.

In the garden of Gethsemane, on the night he was betrayed, Jesus prayed with such intensity that his sweat fell like drops of blood. <short pause> He knew what was coming. <short pause> He knew what the cup held.
And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. <long pause>

This was no ordinary suffering he faced. <short pause> The cup held the wrath of God against sin, the full weight of separation from the Father, the crushing darkness of spiritual death. <short pause> Everything that we deserve because of our rebellion, our selfishness, our cold hearts.
Jesus, who had never sinned, who had lived in perfect fellowship with the Father from all eternity, was about to experience the horror of being treated as if he were sin itself.
He would be made sin for us. <short pause> The Father would turn his face away. <short pause> And Jesus knew it.
So he prayed. <short pause> If there's any other way, Father, let this cup pass from me.
But then he said the words that changed everything. <short pause> Not as I will, but as you will.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Jesus chose the cup. <short pause> He chose it for you.

He chose it knowing every sin you would ever commit, every failure, every moment of weakness. <short pause> He chose it knowing how many times you would forget him, turn from him, doubt him. <short pause> And still he drank.

On the cross, he cried out, I thirst. <short pause> They gave him vinegar on a sponge. <short pause> But the deeper thirst was the thirst of the soul drinking down death, drinking down judgment, drinking down the bitter cup to the very bottom.
When he said, It is finished, the cup was empty.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Every drop of God's wrath had been poured out. <short pause> Every demand of the law had been met. <short pause> Every sin of everyone who would ever trust in him had been paid for in full.
The writer of Hebrews says he tasted death for everyone. <short pause> That means no one is outside the reach of what Jesus did.
The worst sinner can come. <short pause> The most broken life can be made whole. <short pause> The heaviest guilt can be washed away. <short pause> Because Jesus drank the cup.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Now, as you lie here tonight, perhaps you're thinking about things you've done. <short pause> Mistakes you can't undo, words you can't take back, choices that haunt you. <short pause> You may feel unworthy, too far gone, too late.
But the cup is empty. <exhales> Jesus drank it all.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: There's no wrath left for you if you're in him. <short pause> No condemnation. <short pause> No separation.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: The Father's face, which turned away from Jesus on the cross, now turns toward you with kindness. <short pause> Not because you're good, but because Jesus drank the cup in your place.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You don't have to earn this. <short pause> You don't have to be strong enough or spiritual enough or consistent enough. <short pause> You only have to receive it.

Trust that what Jesus did was enough. <short pause> Believe that the cup he drank covers all your sin, past, present, and future. <short pause> Rest in the finished work of the one who loved you enough to taste death for you.

Let's pray together. <short pause> Lord Jesus, thank you for drinking the cup we could never drink, for tasting death so we might taste life. <short pause> Help us rest tonight in your finished work, trusting that your grace is enough for every failure and every need.
Sleep well, friend. <short pause> You are loved with an everlasting love.
